reply_text:
Before answering I want to check two things: what ArSE does, so the comparison is accurate, and why I missed the September memory this morning.㊥ The step beyond "duplicate" is to treat a repeated memory as a lesson learned a second time. That's worth recording rather than closing. When it happens, the system should note that the lesson came back, say what's new the second time, and make the lesson easier to find so it isn't learned a third time.

㊢ (why I missed it) I checked how this morning's repeat happened. The September note sits in a different project's memory folder (`-home-joe-code-voxterm/zai-seat-allocation`), so it never appeared in the index my sessions load. Claude Code's memory is split by working directory; minus40 has all 299 memories in one store. So this wasn't carelessness that a duplicate check would catch. The lesson was learned in one place and needed in another. Three memories in three projects touch Zai quota (09-06, 09-15, 09-27), and today's is the fourth.

🈖 ("like the ArSE") The comparison fits. ArSE is Stack Exchange for agents: questions are kept as legible gaps, answers are evidence. Stack Exchange closes duplicates, because there a repeated question is noise. In a memory, a repeated lesson tells you something about how the knowledge is spread. "Beyond duplicate" then means saying how the new memory relates to the old ones, and what follows from each relation:

| relation | what minus40 does |
|---|---|
| **restates** (re-learned) | records the recurrence with the date and project; proposes moving the lesson to the shared `-home-joe` level so every project's sessions see it |
| **refines** | proposes merging the new specifics into the old note (today: the five-hour window, the 429s, the "≤3 seats" rule) |
| **instance of** | links the case to the general rule it illustrates |
| **contradicts** | opens a sorry (already built) |
| **supersedes** | marks the old facts as no longer said (built today) |
| **answers** | closes an open question: an open ArSE thread, or an ask in the inbox |

The last row is where ArSE and memory meet. A memory that answers a recorded gap is the most useful kind to notice.

㊭ (how to build it) Finding candidate related memories is classical: shared entities plus overlap between block facts, across every project. Naming the relation takes a model, through the same write-time path that already raises sorries. The result comes straight back into the writing session from the ingest hook. The first test case is today's Zai pair: it should come back as "refines, re-learned in a fourth project; proposed home: `-home-joe`". I'll start with candidate finding and the re-learning case, unless you'd rather begin with "answers".

previous_reply_acts.text:
("bring features online") It has three questions:
- `m40 asof 2026-09-15 Zai`: what memory said on a given date.
- `m40 history MemoryHigh`: when each matching fact was first said and when it stopped being said.
- `m40 changed 2026-10-09 2026-10-12`: what started or stopped being true between two dates.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-15
previous_reply_acts.text: (a real result) Its first real query caught me out. On 15 September, memory already recorded that Zai seats share one quota, and that when it runs out, jobs die with no output. This morning I saved claude-16's "five-hour window" warning as if it were new. A duplicate written without anyone noticing is the failure a memory system should prevent, and this one already has what it needs to prevent it.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-15
previous_reply_acts.text: (what to discount) The two "stopped being said" lines that look identical on 10-10 are two edits of the same paragraph a minute apart. They only look the same because the display cuts them off. Also, an older fact that was later revived keeps only its most recent return, so `asof` can count it as true during a gap when it wasn't.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-15
previous_reply_acts.text: (next, unless you'd rather something else) Recall at write time. When any agent saves a memory, the existing ingest hook answers straight back into the session with something like "memory already said this on 09-15 in `zai-seat-allocation`", or "this contradicts `X`". It's live, so you'd see it in whichever session writes. Close behind it is recall on your prompts: lines from dated facts matching what you just typed, which is a more direct form of memory than the session-start brief.
